papers.title: MuJoCo Warp (MJWarp): GPU-optimized version of the MuJoCo physics simulator, designed for NVIDIA hardware
papers.code_status: Apache-2.0; v3.14.0 released 2026-09-22 (PyPI mujoco-warp 3.14.0 same day); repo created 2025-03-17; nightly benchmarks on gh-pages (last MyoArm row 2026-09-03); no technical report found; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: google-deepmind/mujoco_warp: GPU-optimized version of the MuJoCo physics simulator, designed for NVIDIA hardware.
papers.core_idea: Warp re-implementation of MuJoCo for batched simulation on NVIDIA GPUs, optimized for throughput rather than latency. Supports all MJCF actuator, tendon and wrapping types, raises exceptions on unsupported features (e.g., non-zero geom margin with some CCD colliders), and is documented as non-deterministic on GPU.
papers.what_to_take: Size nconmax/njmax, capture CUDA graphs, check Data.overflow. Nightly MyoArm benchmark (63 muscles, 8,192 worlds, RTX 6000 Ada): 1.41M steps/s, 85 s JIT, 1.77 GB; tendon kinematics take ~40% of step time.
papers.left_untested: No CPU-versus-GPU parity for contact-rich muscle models; GPU determinism unsupported in 3.14.0 (API PR #1687 opened 2026-09-22; open PR #1533 lists tendon and actuator-moment accumulations as order-sensitive); nightlies use Ada, not sm_120.
papers.feasibility_notes: Use 3.14.0 on both sides: it includes the IMPLICIT Coriolis-derivative fix (#1663) for a 1.45e12 versus 22.7 rad/s CPU mismatch. Deterministic reference: native MuJoCo.

papers.title: mjlab: A Lightweight Framework for GPU-Accelerated Robot Learning
papers.authors_short: Zakka, Liao, Yi, Le Lay, Sreenath, Abbeel
papers.code_status: Apache-2.0; v1.6.0 (2026-08-09, also on PyPI); pins mujoco and mujoco-warp ~=3.11.0, warp-lang>=1.14, rsl-rl-lib==5.5.1, torch from the cu128 index; main pushed 2026-09-22; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: mjlab: A Lightweight Framework for GPU-Accelerated Robot Learning
papers.core_idea: Pairs Isaac Lab's manager-based API (observations, rewards, events, terminations, curricula) with MuJoCo Warp, exposing native MjModel/MjData, CUDA-graph stepping, per-world randomization, MJCF-wrapped or native actuators including muscles, and NaN/Inf detection with a replayable rolling state buffer.
papers.what_to_take: Its nightly benchmark runs on an RTX 5090 at 4,096 envs: environment-layer overhead is 54-68%; G1 tracking gives 730k physics-only versus 249k full-environment control steps/s (2026-09-23). Use its NaN replay unattended.
papers.left_untested: Scope is rigid-body robots: the paper has no muscle or tendon task, no throughput tables, and no CPU-MuJoCo parity or determinism analysis.
papers.feasibility_notes: Pins mujoco(-warp) ~=3.11 while the probe used 3.14. Issue #1160: headless EGL rendering beside Warp segfaults on sm_120; render in a separate process.

papers.title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
papers.code_status: Not released: v1 (2026-09-17) says the code 'will be made publicly available'; no repository located; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
papers.core_idea: The SMAT authors move human-exoskeleton co-adaptation to MuJoCo Warp with mjlab: an 80-muscle MyoLeg with polynomial knee constraints, a pelvis-rigid belt and compliant sliding thigh cuffs; four imitation experts are distilled into one latent policy, then co-adapted with a bilateral hip controller via MARL.
papers.what_to_take: GPU operating point to copy: 300 Hz physics, 100 Hz policy, rsl_rl PPO, 8,192 envs (human) and 2,048 (co-adaptation), 3.7x10^4 environment steps/s including learning, on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
papers.left_untested: No CPU-versus-GPU physics or policy parity, no rerun of CPU-trained SMAT on the new stack, no 26-muscle myolegs26 model, no training-seed replication, and no physics-versus-learning throughput split.
papers.feasibility_notes: Same sm_120 architecture as the 5090 but 96 GB versus 32 GB VRAM; measure 8,192-env memory before copying. Code not yet released.

papers.title: MyoSuite 3.0 release branch (ms3; pull request #406): CPU Gymnasium and mjlab/MuJoCo Warp backends
papers.authors_short: Caggiano, Hodossy, Fischer, Wang, MyoSuite Team (per ms3 README citation)
papers.code_status: PR #406 (ms3 into dev) open since 2026-09-15, 171 commits; ms3 head 2026-09-23; latest tagged release still v2.12.0 (2026-04-23); mjlab extra: mjlab>=1.4.0, mujoco-warp>=3.7.0, warp-lang>=1.12.0, torch>=2.13.0; checked 2026-09-23
papers.core_idea: Makes CPU Gymnasium and mjlab (MuJoCo Warp) the supported backend pair under one env_id, bound by a five-invariant contract (observation layout, action mapping, control timing, identical XML, fixed normalization); MJX is labelled experimental; myoLegWalk is ported with 403-D observations and 80-D muscle actions.
papers.what_to_take: Adopt its frozen-rollout replay tests and contract. Even CPU-to-CPU replay of myoLegWalk jumps to 4.22e-5 after ~25 steps (contact ordering), so tolerances must be horizon-specific.
papers.left_untested: Its GPU-gated CPU-versus-mjlab myoLegWalk diagnostic asserts only finite, below-50 observation differences ('trajectories need not be identical yet'); no statistical parity, myolegs26 or hip-exoskeleton task.
papers.feasibility_notes: Unreleased: pin a commit. The mjlab extra resolves to mjlab's ~=3.11 MuJoCo pin; the MJX extra caps jax<0.5.3, predating JAX's CUDA 12.8 builds.

papers.title: GPUSimBench: Towards Scalable and Reliable GPU-Accelerated Simulators in Embodied AI
papers.authors_short: Zhang, Yuan, Yan, Ma, Li, Pang, Yudin
papers.code_status: No repository link in v1 (2026-07-06); the text says the benchmark and protocol will be released on a project website, which was not located; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: GPUSimBench: Towards Scalable and Reliable GPU-Accelerated Simulators in Embodied AI
papers.core_idea: Benchmarks seven GPU simulators (Isaac Lab, ManiSkill, Genesis, Madrona, MuJoCo Warp, MJX, MuJoCo Playground) for real-world alignment, scaling and determinism, using Wasserstein-1 distances between final-state distributions across parallel environments and across repeated fixed-seed runs.
papers.what_to_take: Reuse its two metrics, within-run parallel W1 and between-run W1, as a parity template. MuJoCo Warp showed both variabilities (Type 3); MJX showed neither at reported precision (RTX 5070).
papers.left_untested: Rigid cubes and a Panda arm only: no muscles, tendons or gait; no comparison against CPU MuJoCo; MuJoCo Warp version unstated; no formal hypothesis test or tolerance.
papers.feasibility_notes: Metrics are cheap to reproduce on the 5090; add a CPU-MuJoCo ensemble as the reference distribution.

papers.title: A new ensemble-based consistency test for the Community Earth System Model (pyCECT v1.0)
papers.authors_short: Baker, Hammerling, Levy, Xu, Dennis, Eaton, Edwards, Hannay et al.
papers.code_status: Apache-2.0; PyCECT release 3.3.1 (2024-06-14); last push 2026-06-15; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: A new ensemble-based consistency test for the Community Earth System Model (pyCECT v1.0)
papers.core_idea: Replaces bit-for-bit reproducibility with a statistical test: a 151-member ensemble differing only by O(1e-14) initial perturbations defines PCA score distributions of standardized global means; runs from a new platform fail when the same PCs fall outside 2 sigma.
papers.what_to_take: Transferable decision rule: three test runs; fail if at least three PCs exceed 2 sigma in at least two runs (0.5% false-positive rate). Follow-up UF-CAM-ECT (Milroy 2018) needs only nine time steps.
papers.left_untested: Climate model without contacts, discrete events or learned controllers; annual global means must be replaced by gait statistics, and power against small physics bugs must be re-established for locomotion.
papers.feasibility_notes: A ~150-rollout perturbed CPU ensemble is cheap on 64 cores; treat pyCECT as a reference implementation, not a drop-in tool.

papers.title: Towards Embodied AI with MuscleMimic: Unlocking full-body musculoskeletal motor learning at scale
papers.authors_short: Li, Wang, Ziliotto, Simos, Kovecses, Durandau, Mathis
papers.code_status: Apache-2.0; release 'preprint' (2026-09-21), package version 0.1.1; pins mujoco and mujoco-mjx 3.4.0, warp-lang 1.10.0, jax 0.7.2; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: Towards Embodied AI with MuscleMimic: Unlocking full-body musculoskeletal motor learning at scale
papers.core_idea: JAX framework extending LocoMuJoCo for motion imitation with a 126-muscle fixed-root upper-body model and a 416-muscle full-body model on MuJoCo Warp (optional MJX for reduced contacts), plus SMPL retargeting and one generalist policy trained on hundreds of motions.
papers.what_to_take: Scaling curve on one H100: 1,263 SPS at 128 envs, 6,105 at 1,024, 1.3x10^4 at 8,192 (416 muscles); 1B steps in about 20 h. Final GPU policies are re-evaluated on CPU MuJoCo.
papers.left_untested: Backend check is policy-level (consistent metrics, same top-three ablations), not state-trajectory or distributional parity; no exoskeleton or co-adaptation; no consumer-Blackwell numbers.
papers.feasibility_notes: Its jax 0.7.2 pin postdates JAX's CUDA 12.9 builds (sm_120-capable); its mujoco 3.4.0 pin predates later tendon and solver changes.

papers.title: Scaling Whole-Body Human Musculoskeletal Behavior Emulation for Specificity and Diversity
papers.authors_short: Wei, Zuo, Zhuang, Gong, Liu, Sui
papers.code_status: Project page https://lnsgroup.cc/research/MS-Emulator/ shows 'Code Coming Soon'; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: Scaling Whole-Body Human Musculoskeletal Behavior Emulation for Specificity and Diversity
papers.core_idea: Runs the ~700-muscle MS-Human-700 model on MuJoCo Warp, chosen over MJX because active contact and constraint sets vary, and adds adversarial reward aggregation and value-guided flow exploration to emulate walking, running, dance, cartwheels and backflips.
papers.what_to_take: Only RTX 5090 muscle-model numbers found: forward dynamics 7,107 SPS versus 2,469 on 224 CPU cores; training 4,460 SPS on one GPU versus 1,326 for an SB3 CPU baseline; 2 ms step, 50 Hz control.
papers.left_untested: No state-level CPU-versus-GPU trajectory comparison; environment counts behind the SPS figures appear only in plots (training trials used 2,048 envs); code unreleased; no exoskeleton.
papers.feasibility_notes: Direct 5090 evidence: 700 muscles train at ~4.5k SPS; 26- or 80-muscle legs should be faster, but that is unmeasured.

papers.title: msk-warp: MJWarp musculoskeletal differentiation RL environment
papers.code_status: Apache-2.0; no releases; README status dated 2026-09-13; last push 2026-09-23; requires a local stack of unmerged MJWarp PR #1423 (differentiable stepping), MuJoCo 3.10.0, Warp 1.14.0; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: mar-yan24/msk-warp: MJWarp musculoskeletal differentiation RL environment
papers.core_idea: Individual research code for MyoLeg26 (the myolegs26 beta model: nq=47, nv=46, 26 muscles) on MuJoCo Warp that compares native float64 MuJoCo and Warp states at 1, 4 and 16 physics steps and checks simulation gradients against finite differences.
papers.what_to_take: Closest precedent on the programme's model: native-versus-Warp forward cases exceeded a 1e-4 joint-velocity tolerance in 20/50 states after one control step and 45/50 after four; direct-Warp replays varied across repetitions.
papers.left_untested: Self-reported and unreviewed; uses an unmerged MJWarp PR stack, not a release; short horizons only; no ensemble statistics or exoskeleton; its five-seed PPO baseline never walked (0/160 survivors).
papers.feasibility_notes: Ran on an RTX 4060 laptop; reuse its hash-pinned manifests and preregistered gates, not its patched backend.

papers.title: The Accumulation of Rounding Errors and Port Validation for Global Atmospheric Models
papers.api_title: The Accumulation of Rounding Errors and Port Validation for Global Atmospheric Models
papers.core_idea: Studies how machine-rounding-sized differences grow in the NCAR CCM2 climate model and proposes validating ports by checking that port-induced differences grow no faster than rounding-level perturbations of the original code.
papers.what_to_take: Direct recipe for CPU-versus-MJWarp: perturb CPU initial states at float32 rounding scale, record divergence growth curves, then require the GPU-versus-CPU curve to stay inside that envelope over early steps.
papers.left_untested: Baker et al. report it breaks for ill-conditioned CAM5 physics, where tolerances are exceeded within a few steps; contact-rich gait may saturate similarly. No code, contacts or controllers.
papers.feasibility_notes: Cheap (dozens of paired rollouts); use it for short horizons and single swing phases, ensemble tests for full strides.

papers.title: Learning to Walk in Minutes Using Massively Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_status: legged_gym (Isaac Gym; custom licence, no releases) last pushed 2025-05-29; companion PPO library rsl_rl v5.5.1 (2026-09-09) is pinned by mjlab; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: Learning to Walk in Minutes Using Massively Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: Shows that PPO with thousands of parallel simulated robots on one workstation GPU trains ANYmal locomotion in minutes, analyses which algorithm components matter in this massively parallel regime, and adds a game-inspired terrain curriculum; policies transfer to hardware.
papers.what_to_take: Flat terrain in under four minutes, rough in twenty. mjlab and UniExo train with rsl_rl, the PPO library released with it, so re-tune rollout length and minibatching for SMAT at thousands of GPU environments.
papers.left_untested: Rigid quadruped with PD-controlled joints on PhysX; no muscles, multi-agent co-adaptation, simulator parity or determinism analysis.
papers.feasibility_notes: Isaac Gym is superseded by Isaac Lab (legged_gym last pushed 2025-05); take the recipe through rsl_rl in mjlab, not legged_gym.

papers.title: MuJoCo XLA (MJX) documentation
papers.code_status: Part of google-deepmind/mujoco (Apache-2.0); PyPI mujoco-mjx 3.14.0 (2026-09-22); no dedicated MJX paper found; checked 2026-09-23
papers.core_idea: Documents MJX's two implementations: MJX-JAX, a JAX re-implementation supporting muscle dynamics, gain and bias with fixed and spatial tendons, and MJX-Warp, MuJoCo Warp behind the JAX API, supporting all actuator, tendon and wrapping types with faster contacts.
papers.what_to_take: Use MJX-JAX only when JAX autodiff or JAX trainers are required; for NVIDIA throughput prefer MJWarp (humanoid: 3.35M SPS pure Warp versus 2.96M through JAX FFI).
papers.left_untested: The page gives no precision, determinism or MuJoCo-C agreement guarantees and no muscle-model benchmarks; single-scene MJX-JAX can be 10x slower than MuJoCo.
papers.feasibility_notes: JAX CUDA wheels are built with CUDA 12.8+ from jax 0.6.0; test older pins such as MyoSuite's jax<0.5.3 before relying on sm_120.

papers.title: NVIDIA Warp: a Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning
papers.code_status: Apache-2.0; v1.17.0 (2026-08-31), PyPI wheels built with CUDA Toolkit 12.9, CUDA 13.0 wheels on GitHub Releases; deterministic execution modes since v1.15.0 (2026-07-07); checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: NVIDIA/warp: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.
papers.core_idea: Python kernel language that JIT-compiles to CUDA or CPU and underlies MuJoCo Warp and Newton; since v1.15 it offers opt-in deterministic modes (RUN_TO_RUN bit-exact on one GPU architecture, GPU_TO_GPU across architectures) that record, sort and reduce atomics.
papers.what_to_take: Use it for custom deterministic kernels (e.g., reward or statistics reductions); cost depends on atomic contention, and overflows inside CUDA-graph capture go unreported, so size deterministic_max_records conservatively.
papers.left_untested: MJWarp does not support Warp's deterministic mode (maintainer, 2026-09-10; API PR #1687 open); enabling it silently dropped convex contacts (#1635). Determinism costs for muscle models are unmeasured.
papers.feasibility_notes: warp-lang 1.17.0 (CUDA 12.9 wheels) ran on the 5090 in the probe; v1.12.1 fixed crashes when processes share a kernel cache on CUDA 12.8/12.9 builds.

papers.title: MuJoCo Playground
papers.authors_short: Zakka, Tabanpour, Liao, Haiderbhai, Holt, Luo, Allshire, Frey et al.
papers.code_status: Apache-2.0; v0.2.0 (2026-03-16) made MuJoCo Warp the default implementation for all envs; main requires mujoco>=3.6.0, warp-lang>=1.17.0, brax>=0.14.2; checked 2026-09-23
papers.core_idea: Open-source MJX-based robot-learning suite covering quadrupeds, humanoids, dexterous hands and arms, with Madrona batch rendering, JAX PPO training in minutes on one GPU, and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer from state and pixel policies.
papers.what_to_take: Ready A/B harness: the same tasks run with --impl warp under JAX PPO or rsl_rl PPO, and v0.2.0 made MuJoCo Warp the default; throughput tables are per-environment on one A100.
papers.left_untested: No musculoskeletal environments; the paper predates the MuJoCo Warp default; no MJX-versus-MuJoCo-C numerical or statistical comparison.
papers.feasibility_notes: Good for backend A/B checks on rigid tasks; its JAX stack needs CUDA 12.8+ JAX wheels on sm_120.

papers.title: Isaac Lab: A GPU-Accelerated Simulation Framework for Multi-Modal Robot Learning
papers.authors_short: NVIDIA: Mittal, Roth, Tigue, Richard, Zhang, Du et al.
papers.code_status: BSD-3-Clause; v3.0.0-EA (2026-09-16) built for Isaac Sim 6.1, Warp 1.16 and Newton 1.5.2, with kit-less physics=newton_mjwarp; GA targeted end of October 2026; checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: Isaac Lab: A GPU-Accelerated Simulation Framework for Multi-Modal Robot Learning
papers.core_idea: Successor to Isaac Gym combining GPU PhysX, tiled RTX rendering, actuator and sensor models, domain randomization and a manager-based task API; outlines integration with Newton, the Warp-based engine that uses MuJoCo Warp as its primary backend.
papers.what_to_take: Origin of the manager-based API mjlab copies. Isaac Lab 3.0 Early Access (2026-09-16) runs physics=newton_mjwarp without Isaac Sim, a fallback host for MJWarp if mjlab stalls.
papers.left_untested: No muscle or tendon models; MJCF muscle import through Newton is undocumented in the paper; no CPU-MuJoCo parity or determinism study.
papers.feasibility_notes: Full Isaac Sim lists 32 GB minimum RAM (server has 30 GB); only the kit-less Newton path looks practical. GA targeted late October 2026.

cluster_lessons: GPU non-determinism is documented behaviour, not a defect: MJWarp 3.14.0 does not support Warp's deterministic mode (maintainer, 2026-09-10); a maintainer determinism API (PR #1687, DeterminismType flags) opened 2026-09-22, and a community implementation (PR #1422) cost 30-80% throughput. Keep native CPU MuJoCo as the bitwise reference and design parity statistically.

Not every CPU-GPU gap is chaos: MJWarp #1662 (IMPLICIT, 1.45e12 versus 22.7 rad/s, fixed by #1663 before 3.14.0) and #1510 (CCD versus box-box collider behaviour, reproducible in MuJoCo C) were defects or configuration effects. Run contact-free, fixed-collider and deterministic-CPU checks before attributing divergence to chaos.

Published parity evidence for muscle models is weak: UniExo reports none; MuscleMimic compares policy-level metrics; MyoSuite 3's CPU-versus-mjlab myoLegWalk test only bounds observation differences below 50; msk-warp reports 20/50 and 45/50 native-versus-Warp exceedances of 1e-4 after one and four control steps on myolegs26. Even CPU-to-CPU replay of myoLegWalk jumps to 4.22e-5 after ~25 steps.

Borrow port-validation statistics from climate modelling: Rosinski-Williamson perturbation-growth envelopes for early horizons, CESM-ECT ensemble consistency (151 perturbed members, PCA, three test runs, 0.5% false-positive rate) for full strides, with UF-CAM-ECT showing nine-step tests can suffice; GPUSimBench's within-run and between-run W1 metrics are the robotics analogue.

Physics is unlikely to be the binding constraint: the probe reached ~235k control transitions/s physics-only at nworld=8192, mjlab's RTX 5090 nightly spends 54-68% of time in the environment layer, and UniExo's full pipeline sustains 3.7e4 environment steps/s including PPO. Profile physics, environment layer and learner separately.

Muscle-model GPU cost concentrates in tendon kinematics (MJWarp nightly MyoArm: ~40% of per-step time; 1.41M steps/s at 8,192 worlds on an RTX 6000 Ada), so 26- versus 80-muscle legs should scale with tendon count and wrapping more than with DoF.

Blackwell (sm_120) works when every wheel is a CUDA 12.8+ build: warp-lang 1.17 (CUDA 12.9), JAX >= 0.6.0, PyTorch cu128. MyoSuite's MJX extra (jax<0.5.3) predates this, and offscreen rendering beside Warp in one headless process can segfault (mjlab #1160).

Version drift confounds parity and precedent numbers: MuscleMimic pins MuJoCo 3.4.0, mjlab ~=3.11, Newton ~=3.12 and the probe 3.14.0; 3.13-3.14 carry breaking solver and tendon changes (e.g., tendon actuatorfrclimited now defaults to 'auto'). Freeze one release for both the CPU reference and GPU runs.
occupied_claims: SMAT-style human-exoskeleton co-adaptation trained on MuJoCo Warp/mjlab with an 80-muscle MyoLeg and a bilateral hip controller (UniExo, arXiv 2609.19690, September 2026).
GPU (MuJoCo Warp)-trained muscle policies re-evaluated on CPU MuJoCo with consistent metrics and unchanged top ablations (MuscleMimic, arXiv 2603.25544).
A consumer RTX 5090 with MuJoCo Warp out-trains a 224-core CPU cluster on a ~700-muscle whole-body model (MS-Emulator, arXiv 2603.29332).
GPU-batched simulators, including MuJoCo Warp, show run-to-run and inter-environment variability under fixed seeds, quantified with Wasserstein-1 (GPUSimBench, arXiv 2607.13059).
A CPU-Gymnasium/mjlab cross-backend contract with frozen-rollout parity tests for MyoSuite tasks (MyoSuite 3 ms3 branch, PR #406, unreleased).
Bitwise-deterministic MJWarp stepping via sorted contacts, stable constraint rows and deterministic reductions (community PRs #1422/#1533; maintainer PR #1687; all open).
Ensemble-based statistical consistency testing as a replacement for bit-for-bit reproducibility after ports (Baker et al. 2015; Milroy et al. 2018; Rosinski and Williamson 1997).
Massively parallel single-GPU PPO for legged locomotion in minutes (Rudin et al., CoRL 2021).
open_gaps: No published state-level or distributional parity test between CPU MuJoCo and MuJoCo Warp for a contact-rich, muscle-driven leg (myolegs26 or the 80-muscle MyoLeg), with or without an attached exoskeleton.

No ensemble-consistency protocol adapted to gait: choice of summary statistics (stride time and length, GRF peaks, joint-angle and activation profiles, metabolic proxies), perturbation-ensemble design and false-positive calibration for CPU-versus-GPU physics.
No test that CPU-trained SMAT policies (arXiv 2603.07618/2608.00715) behave equivalently on MJWarp, or that MJWarp-trained SMAT policies survive CPU evaluation, at the distribution level.
The contact and parity effect of disabling MULTICCD (needed to load mesh-margin models on MJWarp 3.14.0) is unmeasured; the CPU reference must use the same flag.
Deterministic-mode coverage of tendon and muscle paths in MJWarp, and its throughput cost on muscle models, are unknown (PR #1533 still lists tendon lengths and actuator moments as order-sensitive).
No physics / environment-layer / learner throughput breakdown for muscle-plus-exoskeleton training on a 32 GB consumer Blackwell GPU; UniExo reports one aggregate number on a 96 GB card.
Float32 (GPU) versus float64 (CPU) effects on stiff muscle activation dynamics and tendon wrapping are unquantified for gait.
Sprint regime (80-muscle runner, high speed, impacts) has no GPU-backend parity evidence; MuscleMimic and MS-Emulator track running but report no state-level backend comparison.
unverifiable: MuJoCo Warp technical report or paper: none found (arXiv title search 'MuJoCo' AND 'Warp' returned 0; web search shows it is cited as a GitHub project).
Dedicated MJX paper: none found; MJX is documented only (MuJoCo Playground builds on it).
Newton physics engine paper: none found; only the repository (v1.6.0, 2026-09-10), Isaac Lab paper section 7.1 and the Kamino solver paper (arXiv 2603.16536).
NVIDIA Warp archival paper: none found; it is commonly cited as a 2022 GTC talk (Macklin), which was not verified.
'MyoSuite 3.0 -- A multimodal platform for efficient and scalable musculoskeletal motor control' (arXiv 2026): cited in the ms3 README with placeholder DOI and URL; not on arXiv as of 2026-09-23.
UniExo code: paper says it will be made publicly available; no repository found.
GPUSimBench benchmark code or project website: announced in the paper; no link found.
MuJoCoUni (arXiv 2605.24922) package 'mujoco-uni': not found on PyPI or by GitHub search (paper itself verified; not selected).
That GitHub user Fitz-Yuan is a UniExo author: the profile has no name; the fork itself is verified identical to upstream.
